metadata.description: Personal Claude Code plugin marketplace by Charalampos Kyfonidis

plugins.name: agent-step-toolkit
plugins.description: Build agent-step LangGraph projects and tools: bootstrap a new project (runner library + streaming CLI + scaffold + the required local sandbox service per sandbox-contract.md), define graph state once as a Zod schema (single source of truth for reducers + invoke-boundary validation, channel-completeness enforced at construction; agent-step 2.0.0), localize/override every runner-emitted summary via templated system messages, add domain tools (actions / executors / verifiers / controller hooks + invalidatesOnChange; executors request library-state transitions via typed effects) with sandbox extensions per backend, offer engine-owned one-shot bounded choices with turn-provenance locks, port an existing project onto agent-step, including read-tool patterns (native paginated reads via `pageable`, LLM-authored data analysis over fetched data), channel-handoff actions with orchestrator/specialized agent roles, completed/abandon/off_topic handbacks, and library-coordinated off-topic delegation via agent-step 2.0.0 (the bootstrap scaffold ships the channel middleware wire/streaming contract), offer Kafka run-tracing observability at bootstrap/port time via the companion kafka-observability plugin (/add-kafka-observability), upgrade downstream projects' vendored runner library (/pull-library, which also reports a stale vendored observability library), author params that carry caller-dictated digits with the library's capture primitives (shape rules as refinements so no `pattern` reaches the model-facing schema, spoken-group transcription fields, ambiguous-reading candidate arrays; field wording stays host-owned — agent-step 2.1.0), lay down the three-layer test methodology, and audit a channel middleware implementation against the wire/streaming/handoff contract.

plugins.name: langgraph-plugin
plugins.description: Run and debug LangGraph.js conversations: /run-langgraph-conversation executes a single- or multi-turn test conversation against the local dev server — finding the running instance that serves the project on any port before starting one — and captures the thread, with an opt-in raw SSE streaming capture (token/handoff/custom event order); /follow-langgraph-conversation investigates any thread end-to-end: locates the instance that OWNS the thread, inventories the available monitoring sources (dev-server checkpoint history, LangSmith traces incl. EU/self-hosted endpoints, process/container logs), reads handoff signals and step-batch tool envelopes, and produces root-cause analysis. Discovers ports, owning instances, graph ids, and LangSmith credentials/endpoint from the project's own config and the live environment (langgraph.json, dev script, docker-compose, .env, running processes/containers).

plugins.name: kafka-observability
plugins.description: LangSmith-parity observability over Kafka for any LangGraph.js / LangChain.js agent: /add-kafka-observability installs or upgrades a vendored src/observability/ library that attaches a BaseTracer subclass globally through two redundant paths — the configure hook plus the configure-slot LangSmith's own tracer occupies, so it attaches even on platform runtimes that sever async-context ancestry (one startup() call, zero per-node instrumentation) — and publishes EVERY traced run — graph invocation, LangGraph nodes, LLM calls with full prompts/outputs/token usage, tool runs, errors, trace hierarchy — as start/end events to a Kafka topic (bank-standard envelope keyed by event id, thread_id correlation, zod-validated, secret-redacted, 512KB-truncated) over a bounded non-blocking fire-and-forget producer (librdkafka, acks=all, idempotent, bounded shutdown). By default EVERY run is emitted (full LangSmith parity); apps that have payload-verified which of their runs duplicate root/llm/tool content can opt into run filtering (KAFKA_RUN_FILTER_MODE=allow|deny + run_type:name globs, the name side also matching metadata.langgraph_node; the root run always survives — it carries the full invocation input/final state and is the turn-boundary marker for timeline consumers). Disabled by default (KAFKA_ENABLED); runs alongside LangSmith for parallel validation so LangSmith can be unplugged with no code change. Startup logs one-line attachment diagnostics (core copy, ALS state, injected loader flags) and warns loudly when the runtime forces the fallback path. Intake proposes broker/topic/security defaults discovered from sibling repos in the workspace that already carry the library (propose-only; the user confirms every value). The skill also wires the client dependency, .env.example, deployment settings with Key Vault refs, a test script, and verifies with typecheck + the library's unit suite. Detects pre-existing Kafka functionality first (foreign src/observability/ modules, producers elsewhere) and asks the user to classify it — agent-flow observability (keep-both or replace with downstream sign-off) vs unrelated e.g. liveness/business events (always preserved) — never overwriting a foreign module.
